## India: Regulatory & Operational Updates

The Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology (MeitY) has officially invited applications for the Chairperson and members of the Data Protection Board, a crucial step toward fully operationalizing the Digital Personal Data Protection Act (DPDPA). This move addresses concerns about the Board's vacancy and its impact on the DPDPA's enforcement and adjudication functions.
([Source](https://community.nasscom.in/operationalisation-of-the-data-protection-board-meity-invites-applications-for-chairperson-and-members-of-the-board/)) ([Source](https://news.google.?oc=5))

MeitY is also actively seeking industry feedback on proposals to potentially reduce the DPDPA compliance timelines, signaling the government's intent to accelerate the implementation of the new data protection framework. This initiative highlights a push for quicker adaptation across sectors.
([Source](https://news.google.?oc=5))

The Digital Personal Data Protection Act (DPDPA) 2023 has officially been brought into force, establishing a new comprehensive legal framework for personal data handling in India. This marks a pivotal moment for data privacy regulations, affecting all entities processing the personal data of Indian citizens.

## India: Compliance Challenges & Sectoral Impact

Concerns are growing over the readiness of government ministries, state bodies, and startups to meet DPDPA compliance requirements, with discussions highlighting potential director exposure for non-adherence. The Act's broad scope necessitates significant operational adjustments across both public and private sectors.
